# nel-course

A template for **evolving a document by critique**: one artifact, one Markdown
source, three outputs, improved one round at a time by a panel of independent
reviewers whose findings are reconciled into a single ranked docket.

Clone it, replace the content in `sections/`, and run `/round`.

> **[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) is the method.** How a round works, why the reviewers
> are independent, what the two registers of a section are for, and the
> guardrails — all of it lives there, in one file. This README only covers
> getting the toolchain running and starting a project.

---

## What you get

```
sections/           the source — one pair of files per section
personas/           the reviewer panel, plus the aggregator
rounds/             committed critique history: one folder per round
site/               the website's template and stylesheet
figures/            figures, referenced from the prose
topic.md            the proposal — what this tutorial is and promises
metadata.yaml       title, authors, and the declared audience
justfile            every build recipe
```

| | Command | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Document | `just doc` | `output/document.pdf` |
| Presentation | `just slides` | `output/slides.pdf` |
| Website | `just site` | `_site/index.html` |

`just build` makes all three. `just serve` previews the site locally.

## Setup

Install the toolchain. On macOS:

```
brew install pandoc just librsvg
brew install --cask mactex-no-gui
```

On Debian or Ubuntu:

```
sudo apt-get install -y pandoc just texlive-xetex texlive-latex-extra \
                        texlive-fonts-recommended librsvg2-bin
```

Then confirm it works before changing anything:

```
just build
```

The placeholder content renders, so a failure here is a toolchain problem, not
your writing.

## Start your project

1. **Say what you are doing.** Fill in [topic.md](topic.md) — the proposal: what
   the topic is, why it belongs in this course, what the reader will be able to
   do afterwards, and what is out of scope. Every reviewer reads it, and the
   panel judges the tutorial against it.
2. **Declare your reader.** Edit [metadata.yaml](metadata.yaml) — the title, the
   authors, and especially `audience`. The pedagogy reviewer judges the document
   against whatever you write there, so a vague audience buys you a vague review.
3. **Write.** Replace the placeholders in `sections/`. Each section is a pair:
   `<name>.prose.md` ships, `<name>.concepts.md` holds the spine behind it.
   Section order is the numeric filename prefix — add a section by adding a
   numbered pair.
4. **Check it renders.** `just build`.
5. **Run a round.** `/round` in Claude Code. It produces a ranked docket at
   `rounds/round-NNN/SYNTHESIS.md` and stops; you decide what to act on.

## Publishing

The site deploys to GitHub Pages on demand — never automatically on push.

One-time, in the repository settings: **Settings -> Pages -> Source: GitHub
Actions**. Then:

```
git push
just deploy
```

CI installs the toolchain and runs `just build`, so it publishes exactly what
`just serve` showed you. Nothing generated is stored in git.

## Derived from

The `nel-operator` engine, reduced to its teaching core. The section-pair
convention, the reviewer-panel critic, and the never-reverted single manuscript
come from there; the compile and metrics gates, the archive, the scaffolder, and
the unattended loop deliberately do not.

1	# nel-course — one Markdown source, three outputs.
2	#
3	# Everything is built by pandoc from `sections/*.prose.md`. There is no engine
4	# and no generator: the file list is a shell glob, so the numeric prefixes on the
5	# section filenames ARE the document order. Add a section by adding a numbered
6	# pair; nothing needs to be registered anywhere.
7	#
8	# CI runs these same recipes (see .github/workflows/pages.yml), so there is one
9	# definition of how each output is built and no second copy to drift.
10	
11	outdir := "output"
12	site   := "_site"
13	pandoc := "pandoc"
14	engine := "xelatex"
15	
16	# `open` is macOS. On Linux:  just open=xdg-open view-doc
17	open   := "open"
18	
19	# Shared across all three outputs.
20	common := "--metadata-file=metadata.yaml --resource-path=.:figures --citeproc --bibliography=references.bib"
21	
22	# Print available recipes (default).
23	default:
24	    @just --list
25	
26	# Build all three outputs.
27	build: doc slides site
28	
29	# --- Document ---------------------------------------------------------------
30	
31	# output/document.pdf — the long-form read.
32	doc:
33	    mkdir -p {{outdir}}
34	    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
35	        --pdf-engine={{engine}} \
36	        --toc --toc-depth=2 --number-sections \
37	        -V documentclass=article -V fontsize=11pt -V geometry:margin=1in \
38	        -o {{outdir}}/document.pdf
39	
40	# --- Presentation -----------------------------------------------------------
41	
42	# output/slides.pdf — every `##` heading becomes one slide.
43	slides:
44	    mkdir -p {{outdir}}
45	    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
46	        --pdf-engine={{engine}} \
47	        -t beamer --slide-level=2 \
48	        -o {{outdir}}/slides.pdf
49	
50	# Overflowing slides are not a build problem to work around. They are the
51	# clearest signal you have that a `##` unit is carrying more than one idea, and
52	# the `visual` reviewer is briefed to report them as writing findings. Fix the
53	# prose, not the font size.
54	#
55	# Nothing here checks for you: pandoc hides the TeX log unless the build fails.
56	# Look at the deck, or ask the agent to.
57	
58	# --- Website ----------------------------------------------------------------
59	
60	# The page links to both PDFs, so this depends on them; without that, a local
61	# preview has two dead links that only show up after deploying.
62	
63	# _site/ — one page, sidebar table of contents, both PDFs linked.
64	site: doc slides
65	    mkdir -p {{site}}
66	    {{pandoc}} sections/*.prose.md {{common}} \
67	        --standalone --toc --toc-depth=2 \
68	        --template=site/template.html \
69	        --css=style.css \
70	        -o {{site}}/index.html
71	    cp site/style.css {{site}}/
72	    cp {{outdir}}/document.pdf {{outdir}}/slides.pdf {{site}}/
73	    mkdir -p {{site}}/figures
74	    cp -R figures/. {{site}}/figures/
75	    rm -f {{site}}/figures/README.md
76	
77	# Serve the site locally at http://localhost:8000.
78	serve: site
79	    python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory {{site}}
80	
81	# --- Viewing ----------------------------------------------------------------
82	
83	# Open the document PDF.
84	view-doc: doc
85	    {{open}} {{outdir}}/document.pdf
86	
87	# Open the presentation PDF.
88	view-slides: slides
89	    {{open}} {{outdir}}/slides.pdf
90	
91	# --- Publishing -------------------------------------------------------------
92	
93	# Builds in CI from whatever is on `main` — so commit and push first.
94	# Requires `gh auth login`, and Pages set to "GitHub Actions" in the
95	# repository settings.
96	
97	# Publish the site and both PDFs to GitHub Pages, on demand.
98	deploy:
99	    gh workflow run pages.yml
100	    @echo "Deploy started. Watch it with:  gh run watch"
101	
102	# --- Housekeeping -----------------------------------------------------------
103	
104	# Remove all build outputs.
105	clean:
106	    rm -rf {{outdir}} {{site}}

The "Examples" section is in place as section 4, between Content and Conclusion, and `just build` succeeds from a clean state: the document PDF, the slides PDF and the site all render with the new order.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `sections/04-examples.prose.md` | New — the shipped section, with three `##` units: *A complete example*, *A contrasting example*, *Try it yourself* |
| `sections/04-examples.concepts.md` | New — the spine, with the same five headings as the other sections |
| `sections/04-conclusion.*` → `sections/05-conclusion.*` | Renamed, contents untouched |
| `topic.md` | `04-conclusion` → `05-conclusion`, "four sections" → "five sections", and a mention of `04-examples` under Shape |

Nothing is committed; the changes are unstaged in the working tree.

## Choices I made

- **Renumbered the conclusion rather than using an in-between prefix.** Order comes from the numeric filename prefix, so the conclusion moved to `05`. Git will show this as a delete plus an add until the files are staged, at which point it detects the rename.
- **Wrote the section as template placeholders, not real content.** The other sections are all guidance blockquotes plus "Replace this paragraph.", so the new one matches that.
- **Kept Examples distinct from Content.** Content already has two walkthroughs, so the guidance frames Examples as whole, realistic cases that introduce nothing new, ending with an exercise for the reader.
- **Left the README, personas and `/round` skill alone.** None of them hardcode the section list or count.

## Things you should know

- **`CLAUDE.md` is missing.** The README calls it "the method" and links to it, but it isn't in the repository. I followed the conventions from the README, the `justfile` comments and the existing sections instead.
- **The title slide overflows, and did before my change.** xelatex reports the title slide as about 45pt too tall, identically with and without the new section. The new Examples slides add no overflow warnings.
